q: Warm-up 1. What is the 3rd m.sg. Peal perfect of ܟܬܒ, and what does it mean?
opts: Correct: the bare root with the a-a pattern.
That is 3 f.sg.; the 3 m.sg. has no suffix.
That is the participle, not the perfect.

q: Warm-up 2. Which list gives the three states of the Syriac noun?
opts: Syriac nouns have no case endings; states do that work.

q: Warm-up 3. Translate: ܗܘ ܪܒܐ ܗܘ (hū rabbā hū)
opts: Correct: a verbless clause, the second hū acting as copula.
The second hū is the copula, not a relative clause.

q: Warm-up 4. What is the Peal active participle m.sg. of ܐܙܠ (ʾ-z-l, 'go')?
opts: The m- prefix belongs to derived-stem participles, not the Peal.
The -ā ending marks the f.sg. participle.

q: Warm-up 5. Identify the form ܟܬܒܬ (ketbat).
opts: Root k-t-b, Peal perfect, 3 f.sg., 'she wrote'
Correct: -at is the 3 f.sg. ending. (Unvocalized, ܟܬܒܬ can also be 2 m.sg. or 1 c.sg.; the vowels ketbat settle it.)
The Aphel would add the ʾa- prefix.
The final ܬ is a suffix, not a root letter.

q: What basic meaning does the Aphel stem add to a root?
Which stem in Hebrew and Arabic corresponds to the Syriac Aphel?
opts: Hebrew Hiphil and Arabic Form IV
Correct: all three are causative, and the Arabic ʾa- prefix is cognate.
Hebrew Piel and Arabic Form II
Hebrew Qal and Arabic Form I
Hebrew Niphal and Arabic Form VII

q: The root ܐܠܦ means 'learn' in the Peal. What does it mean in the Aphel?
opts: That would be an intensive sense, not causative.

q: What prefix marks the participle in all the Syriac derived stems?
opts: Correct: maʾlep 'teaching'. A non-Peal verb starting with m- is probably a participle.
n- is an imperfect prefix (1 c.pl.).

q: Give the meaning of ܡܐܠܦܝܢ (maʾlpīn).
opts: Correct: Aphel participle with the m.pl. ending -īn.
The emphatic m.pl. would end in -ē.

q: Which word means 'faith'?
ܩܝܡܐ (qyāmā) carries a double meaning. What are the two?
In the story, what did Yukhannan say the Lord sent him to do?
opts: To teach the people the way of life (ʾūrḥā d-ḥayye)
To baptize the people in the river
The story does not mention baptism.
To build a church in the wilderness

q: Which Aphel verbs does Yukhannan use for God's actions in sentences 3–5?
opts: These do not appear in his speech.

q: How does Yukhannan identify himself to the man from the crowd?
opts: As the servant of the Lord (ʿabdeh d-Māryā)
As a prophet from the wilderness
He mentions the wilderness, but calls himself a servant.
As a teacher of the law

q: According to sentence 11, who gave Yukhannan life and brought him near the kingdom?
opts: Correct: note the feminine verbs ʾaḥyat, ʾaqrebtnī, agreeing with rūḥā.

q: Exercise 1. Identify ܐܠܦ (ʾalep).
opts: Aphel perfect 3 m.sg. of ʾ-l-p: 'he taught'
Peal perfect 3 m.sg. of ʾ-l-p: 'he learned'
The doubled l and ʾa- show the Aphel.
The participle has the m- prefix: maʾlep.

q: Exercise 1. Identify ܡܐܠܦ (maʾlep).
opts: The Peal participle has no m- prefix.

q: Exercise 1. Identify ܟܬܒ when vocalized kāteb.
opts: Peal participle m.sg. of k-t-b: 'writing, writer'

q: Exercise 1. Which of these is Peal, not Aphel?
Exercise 3. Translate: ܝܘܚܢܢ ܐܠܦ ܠܬܠܡܝܕܘܗܝ (Yukhannan ʾalep l-talmīdāw-hy)
opts: l- marks the disciples as the object.
The perfect is past, and -āw-hy is plural.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: ܗܘ ܐܦܩ ܠܗܘܢ ܡܢ ܒܝܬ ܐܣܘܪܐ (Hū ʾappeq lhūn men bēt ʾesūrā)
opts: He brought them out of prison.
He went out of the prison.
That would be Peal; the Aphel is causative.
They brought him out of prison.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: ܡܪܝܐ ܐܩܪܒܢ ܠܡܠܟܘܬܗ (Māryā ʾaqrebnān l-malkūtteh)
opts: The Lord brought us near to his kingdom.
The Lord drew near to his kingdom.
We brought the Lord to his kingdom.
The Lord offered us his kingdom.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: ܐܢܬ ܐܪܝܡܬ ܠܥܒܕܟ (ʾAnt ʾrīmt l-ʿabdāḵ)
Exercise 3. Translate: ܗܢܘ ܐܘܠܦܢܐ ܕܡܠܟܘܬܐ (Hannū ʾūlpānā d-malkūttā)
opts: This is the teaching of the kingdom.
Correct: ʾūlpānā is the abstract noun from ʾalep.
There is no finite verb here.

q: Exercise 4. Which is the best Syriac for 'The Spirit brought him out of the wilderness'?
opts: Correct: Aphel of the root meaning 'go out', with the object suffix.
That is the Peal: 'the Spirit went out'.
That says 'brought him near to the wilderness'.
That says 'the Spirit sent from the wilderness'.

q: Exercise 4. Which is the best Syriac for 'The Lord exalted the humble'?
opts: That says the humble exalted the Lord.
